snapshot_note: v0.53.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 - `-static-libmadc` now works in the .o LINK lane, lifting forest-carriers S5's last stated boundary. The AOT ledger is carried as MIR modules, so the pieces a program needs are pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the same builder as the .o inputs. Through the merge deliberately: a builder's symbol table is append-only (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes by name), and the unification that turns the inputs' UNDEF entries into references to the runtime's definitions IS the merge - so the runtime rides the ONE unification implementation, on the read-back path both containers (ELF ET_REL and MH_OBJECT) already gate. No new format code, no fork change. Generalized rather than duplicated: cir_ledger_pull takes a SEED list (the builder's UNDEF names join the module imports under the same not-defined filter), and the cover analysis takes the reference LIST rather than its source (source lanes pass context imports, the .o lane passes MIR_object_undef_name) - same classifier, same two diagnostics. Fixed on the way: the AOT-ledger carrier now opens HEADER-ONLY (the ledger is a container-global segment, but the probe ran complete_open, which binds the frozen string pool and arena into LIVE parse state - it died with 'forest thaw requires a live string pool' in a lane with no lexer). New -fno-eval-shims: every .o carries __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose twelve madc_value_* imports are Tier B, an executable emit from source skips them and a .o cannot know, so the build says it (the -fPIC shape). live_handoff: SESSION 2026-07-27 #14: _Pragma LANDED; libc++ <type_traits> WORKS; the remaining blockers are CORE-C++ defects, not libc++ ones. Branch feature/libcxx-flavor-claude @7edd7b0b (NOT merged, NOT released — no release obligation until it merges). READ THIS ENTRY, THEN docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md, whose "The real worklist (2026-07-27, verified by reducer at HEAD)" section is the actionable list and carries the localization for item 1. === 1. WHAT LANDED. @7edd7b0b slice 3: _Pragma("...") — the C99/C++11 token form of #pragma. handle_pragma_body() is now the ONE implementation, entered with `source` positioned at the pragma text; the #pragma directive arrives already positioned and handle_pragma_operator() destringizes into the same stream before calling it. Because the body was ALREADY text-driven, the operator needed no copy of the pack/push_macro handling — which was the whole constraint, since those two are pragmas madc genuinely ACTS on. The extraction was verified byte-faithful (152 lines, identical modulo indentation) before building, so the directive path provably did not shift. THREE DECISIONS: (a) the operand is read as a TOKEN, not characters, because the standard macro-expands it first and libc++ writes both _Pragma(#x) and _Pragma(_LIBCPP_TOSTRING(clang diagnostic ignored str)) — going through the lexer buys that expansion, and its string case has already undone \" and \\, so the token text IS the destringized pragma line with no second unescaper to drift; (b) the pushed-back text is NEWLINE-TERMINATED and that is load-bearing — every handler branch ends by discarding the rest of its directive line, so without a terminator the discard runs off the pushback and eats real code (pushed-back newlines do not advance the line counter, so __LINE__ is unaffected, and the test pins it); (c) NOT gated on --std= — both canons accept _Pragma in every mode including -std=c89 -pedantic, and the name is reserved to the implementation. It sits after the define_map check so a user `#define _Pragma …` still wins, same as __FILE__/__LINE__. === 2. EVIDENCE. 757 passed / 0 failed / 0 timed out / 9 skipped JIT, EXE 741/0, OBJ 741/0, libcxx_gate OK. The +1 in each lane is exactly the test this commit adds (was 756/740/740). tests/testpragmaoperator.mad is an ORDINARY integration test, not a libc++ gate leg, because _Pragma is standard C; it asserts that the directive and operator spellings AGREE (pack(1) written both ways), plus push_macro/pop_macro, the DO_PRAGMA(x) stringize idiom, an ignored unknown pragma, several _Pragma calls expanded inline from one macro (the libc++ shape), and __LINE__. madc, gcc and clang print it byte-identically. === 3. THE HEADLINE, AND A CORRECTION I MADE MID-SESSION. libc++'s <type_traits> COMPILES AND ITS TRAITS EVALUATE CORRECTLY: std::is_same<int,int>, std::is_same<int,long> and std::is_class<Plain> all match the clang oracle. I had earlier recorded that libc++'s std:: names "do not register at all" — THAT WAS WRONG, and it is worth knowing how it was wrong: every probe I wrote spelled the value as `(int)std::is_same<...>::value`, and the CAST was the thing failing, not the lookup. It cost a chain of four dead-end hypotheses (inline namespaces, attributed namespaces, attributed class heads, skipped #if guards) — all four eliminated by reducer, all four innocent. LESSON: when a probe fails, reduce the PROBE before theorizing about the library. === 4. THE REAL WORKLIST (all reducer-verified at HEAD; full detail in the plan doc). (1) `(T)X::y` — a C-style cast with a qualified-name operand — fails to parse; highest value because it masks everything else and is the universal spelling for trait use. LOCALIZED: the cast operand routes to Program::parsePostfixChain(), whose tkNS block at parser.cpp:19675 was written for exactly this (its comment cites `(int)Size::Large`) but resolves only NAMESPACE and scoped-enum qualifiers; a CLASS qualifier falls through to findVariable("S") and dies "undeclared identifier 'S'". Proof of the split: `(int)N::n` with `namespace N` works, `(int)S::n` with `struct S` does not. The missing arm is symmetric with the one above it and needs no new machinery — resolve_expression_class_scope() maps the qualifier to a DataDefCLASS, and resolve_class_static_member_type()/resolve_class_static_member_const_value() turn the member into a typed value, the same pair parsePostfixChain already calls at :19738 for the implicit enclosing-class case. Fixing it there rather than in the cast branch fixes all ~10 callers. CAUTION: do NOT resolve every static through the const-value pair — it returns 0 for a storage-backed member, which would spread defect (2)'s silent wrong answer; either resolve those to their TokenVar or restrict the arm to compile-time constants and let the rest keep erroring. `(int)(S::n)` already works (parens route to the generic branch) — that is the workaround and also why this hides. (2) OUT-OF-LINE STATIC DATA MEMBER DEFINITIONS ARE NOT BOUND: `struct S { static int n; }; int S::n = 5;` then reading S::n yields 0 — a SILENT WRONG VALUE, the most dangerous of the five — and `S::n = 9` fails "lvalue required as left operand of assignment". In-class `static const int n = 5;` works, and `enum { n = 5 };` members work, so the gap is specifically the out-of-line definition. (3) `&S::n` reports "Unknown namespace 'S'" — probably the same parse path as (1); confirm, do not assume. (4) std::is_destructible yields the wrong answer, which is what makes is_trivially_destructible wrong (libc++ defines it as `is_destructible<_Tp>::value && __has_trivial_destructor(_Tp)`). madc's OWN __has_trivial_destructor is CORRECT — 1/0/1 on trivial/non-trivial/int, matching g++ exactly — so the defect is upstream of the intrinsic, in the SFINAE/declval chain. This is the genuine template-metaprogramming burn-down the plan predicted; note __utility/declval.h only became reachable once _Pragma landed. (5) <limits> needs __builtin_nans/nansf/nansl. madc has the QUIET trio and __builtin_inf*/__builtin_huge_val* in the same macro_map block — do NOT alias the signaling ones to (0.0/0.0), that is a quiet NaN and would make numeric_limits<T>::signaling_NaN() silently wrong; a signaling NaN is a distinct bit pattern used in constant expressions, so it is a real question, not a table entry to copy from its neighbour. Items 1-3 are core-C++ defects owing nothing to libc++; the track keeps paying out that way, which is the argument for treating it as C++ conformance work that libc++ merely measures. === 5. SETTLED, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE. libc++ is a LIBRARY not a platform (Apple, Android NDK, FreeBSD, clang-on-Linux) — selected by -stdlib=, never by "is the target Apple"; the library work develops and gates ON LINUX against libc++-18-dev with clang++-18 as oracle, and only target plumbing needs a Mac. Sizes/layouts come from the parse, never a baked table. No embedded libc++ subset. === 6. TRAPS. Piping a compiler through `| head -N` can SIGPIPE-kill the compile, which reads as a build failure that never happened — it briefly had me believing g++ rejects an attributed template head (it does not). The NAS tree and the container tree are SEPARATE (rsync via scripts/remote_build.sh sync); a reducer written on the NAS is invisible to the container, so write it over ssh or sync first. Grepping a build log for "error" matches madc_error.o. === 7. STATE. develop @9af72c00 = v0.53.0, master @277dc086 = v0.48.0, fork @ba216dea = 1.0-madc.0.52.0 UNCHANGED. Feature branch pushed @7edd7b0b. Working tree clean at handoff.

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
